verdict.rationale: Phoenix's first-party docs say you can rerun datasets through different versions of your app, compare evaluation results on the same inputs, and compare examples against prior runs to tell whether an update is an improvement or a regression. The playground also explicitly compares prompt configurations and responses. Missing for 10: detailed documentation of a side-by-side experiment-comparison view with regression diffing, and independent or hands-on corroboration of the comparison workflow.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, I can compare eval runs side by side to catch regressions between prompt or model versions

citations.quote: You can group traces into datasets, rerun them through different versions of your application, and compare evaluation results to confirm whether a change actually improved performance.
Understand whether an update is an improvement or a regression; Drill down into good / bad examples; Compare specific examples vs. prior runs
optimize your app with experiments that compare changes on the same inputs
Comparing prompt configurations and responses in the Phoenix playground
The examples collected are used to run experiments and evaluations to track improvements to your prompt, LLM, or other parts of your LLM application.
